parity_notes: Frozen surfaces untouched: session JSONL rows identical across arms (role/type sequences asserted), RLM wire, prompts, TUI output bytes; the worker recovery journal's compacted bytes are the same records rewrite_records always wrote (the batched-vs-sequential byte oracle from #2936 still passes; the new unit oracles pin the settle-compaction, the batched-settle restore identity, and the unchanged-verdict no-compact). The fresh-write class (append write+fsync — every record durable before the caller proceeds) is UNTOUCHED: 9 journal fsyncs per 4-turn session in every arm. The compact is GC over already-durable records: a lost compact falls back to the append-only history, which replays identically (latest-per-session + latest-snapshot semantics unchanged; read_interrupted/latest_busy_recorded_at/queue restore unchanged). The Finalize seam now encodes each owner's sync class: RetryBusy (command journal, TS writeFileAtomicSync fsync:true) keeps its fsync+rename_onto; Synced (the Rust-native terminal-compaction journal, no TS counterpart) keeps its belt; Bare (the worker journal, TS worker-recovery-journal compact = writeFileSync+renameSync, NO fsync) is the TS shape — temp write+rename, no fsync. The CENSUSED TS anatomy confirms the TS compact class in-product: 1 rename (39us), 0 temp fsyncs. Disclosed TS-parity wrinkles: (a) TS records at EVERY RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT event (~9-10 appends+fsyncs per turn, 39 per 4-turn session — the Rust port's #2936-era checkpoint sites are deliberately leaner at 2 per turn, untouched here); (b) TS's busy computation holds true through turn_end/agent_end (its journal never goes idle in-session — the port's settle records busy=false, a deliberately tighter crash window), so TS's compact fires rarely in practice (once per session at the 'ready' record in the censused trials) while the port — with the TS gate mechanism over the port's own settle sites — compacts at every changed-idle settle; each compact is a 2-line page-cache write + a 31-50us rename (0 fsyncs), so the port's compaction is bounded-GC cost, and the port's journal is bounded where its own idle-at-settle evidence demands it. The probe-prefix leftover 'Zq7bench hello' protocol class from the warm-fsync lane carries over verbatim (disclosed, same erase_all class).

outcome: POSITIVE (both named-waste classes confirmed, quantified, and removed; the barrier anatomy itself was already at the #2936 floor — the honest-negative side is explicit). (1) THE NEVER-FIRE: the worker recovery journal's all-idle gate ran BEFORE the record insert, so the session's own busy admission record blocked every settle's compaction on the dominant single-session shape — the compact NEVER fired and the journal grew append-only for the session's lifetime (censused: 17 lines/3.9KB per 4-turn session, 97 lines/21.6KB per 24-turn session, zero compaction events in every baseline trial; a day-one port divergence from TS's post-insert gate, f492609c6). The candidate restores the TS gate mechanism: the compaction fires at every changed-idle record and the journal stays bounded (2 lines/401B per session, censused in-product). (2) THE REDUNDANT SYNC ON THE COMPACT PATH: where the compact fires, its temp sync_all was a sync class TS's compact does not pay (TS: writeFileSync+renameSync — no fsync; confirmed in-product on TS 0.9.6: 1 rename at 39us, zero temp fsyncs). The C-arm (the naive gate fix that keeps the sync) priced the redundant class in-product: 96.26/99.29/99.33/102.87ms per settle's compact fsync under the host's labeled CLASS-D deep-trap band (36-75ms in the morning phase's bench-context draws; 0.3-0.5ms amortized in healthy windows) — while the candidate's compacts ride the TS class: 4 renames per 4-turn session at 31-50us, ZERO fsyncs. The fresh-write class is untouched in every arm (9 journal fsyncs per session), the #2936 batch intact. (3) THE HONEST NEGATIVE: the settle path's barrier count at base was already minimal (2 journal fsyncs per warm turn, one per #2936 checkpoint batch; there is NO unbatched pair left on the settle path — the task's first candidate class does not exist here); and the settle tail is POST-VISIBLE work (the driver-visible settle metric is parity across arms within noise: A 667.9 / B 668.2 / C 667.2ms p50) — NO latency claim is made; the value is structural: TS-parity behavior (bounded journals; the compaction the #2936 test comment already described), the redundant sync class removed where compacts fire, and the boot/open parse tax bounded (the grown-journal boot legs: 97-line and 3880-line journals boot within the noise floor of the 2-line journal — the growth was an unboundedness defect, not a near-term boot cliff; disclosed).
